clue.text: Blanket a requirement in poor weather

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, covering everything in a group, as in a catch-all term
the thing you need to carry to keep the rain off

explanation.surface: Someone insists a blanket is essential kit when the weather turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella term is a blanket term covering many things, and an umbrella is the obvious item to take out in rain.

clue.text: Some gas to release blocks large outlet

indicators.note: the run of words holds the answer within itself, as if blocking it in

explanation.surface: Some gas being let out shuts down a big shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocks' is the signal: the letters run through soME GAS TO RElease. 'Some' looks like a quantity word but is part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastore is a very big retail shop, an outlet on a large scale.

clue.text: Bum around, penning English poem

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece is held inside the other
bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the word around is wrongly assembled

explanation.surface: A layabout wanders about while writing an English poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as a noun, a tramp, but is the slang adjective 'bad' signalling an anagram of AROUND, giving RONDAU; 'penning' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain, a kind of poem.

clue.text: Point carried by spike, as weapon

indicators.note: a thing carried by another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to spike a drink is to lace it with alcohol
N, north, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A sharp tip borne on a spike serves as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spike' looks like a noun matching 'Point', but it is the verb: to spike a drink is to lace it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight, a weapon.

clue.text: Trimmed grass — bristle from it?

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, here losing the opening letter

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass

explanation.surface: Cut grass leaves a stiff hair behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition points back to grass: the answer is a bristle growing on grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the stiff hairlike spike on the ear of barley or other grasses.

clue.text: Tickled pink?

definitions.meaning: fish tickling is a way of catching this fish by hand in a river
a shade of orange-pink named after the colour of this fish's flesh

explanation.definitionFit: Poachers catch this fish by tickling its belly, and its flesh gives its name to a pinkish colour.

clue.text: Start to sketch donkey on packet, obscuring device

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey
a packet, like a bomb, is slang for a large sum of money

explanation.surface: An artist begins drawing a donkey on a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is old British slang for a donkey, and both 'packet' and 'bomb' are British slang for a lot of money, as in 'cost a bomb'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke bomb releases a cloud that hides movement, a device for obscuring things.

clue.text: Boy holds map showing Santa's home

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A boy has a map showing where Father Christmas lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland in Finland is popularly said to be where Father Christmas lives.

clue.text: Then everything in effect is like an egg?

annotationWithheld.why: Then everything in effect is like an egg? (5): the only parse is a reverse reading of the whole phrase 'Then everything in effect' as O + VOID ('nothing void'), which the check refuses (reversePhrase), and a cd is refused as a downgrade of that reverse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Then everything in effect is like an egg?

clue.text: Opposed to taking a drink

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone is against having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of against, meaning hostile to something.

clue.text: Fool, in company with politician, getting stuck into no work

indicators.note: the group is pushed inside the word no

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: An idiot hangs around a politician while avoiding any work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stuck into' places the three short pieces inside the negative word; 'in company' reads as 'accompanying', but each word gives letters separately. OP is short for opus.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a silly person, an idiot.

clue.text: Solemnly say when always breaking stuff

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: one word breaks into another, sitting inside it

parts.note: to stuff oneself is to sate
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone declares gravely that they keep smashing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like a noun, things being broken, but it is the verb: to stuff is to SATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to declare earnestly or affirm solemnly.

clue.text: Old charity home left feeding army on ground

indicators.note: a letter feeding into a group goes inside it
ground means crushed, so the words army and on are broken up

explanation.surface: Leftovers are given to troops out in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' (crushed) gives the anagram AMONRY; 'feeding' puts L inside. 'on ground' reads as 'on land', but 'ground' is the anagram signal. An almonry was often part of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: An almonry was a place where alms were handed out to the poor, often attached to a monastery.

clue.text: Facilitate a work of grand proportions

parts.note: to aid is to help or facilitate

explanation.surface: Helping along an enormous project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' hints at grand opera: the work is Verdi's spectacular opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Aida is a famously lavish grand opera, a musical work on a huge scale.

clue.text: Stone managed to cut fish? I'm not sure

indicators.note: one piece cuts into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: cod is a fish
to run a business is to manage it
um is a hesitant sound of uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a fish could be cut with a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Corundum is a hard mineral, aluminium oxide, whose gem forms are ruby and sapphire.

clue.text: Protective sheet starts to unfurl several times coming into port

indicators.note: the opening letters go into the port's name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Dover is a port on the English Channel

indicators.note: the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A sail is unfurled several times as a ship enters harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is a major ferry port in south-east England; 'starts to' takes U, S, T and C, and 'into' puts them inside DOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust cover is a sheet laid over furniture to protect it from dust.

clue.text: Many starving with borders inaccessible

indicators.note: the outermost letters of the word cannot be reached, so they are removed

parts.note: foodless means without food, starving

explanation.surface: Many people are starving and the frontiers are closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with borders inaccessible' removes the first and last letters of FOODLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles means lots, a great many.

clue.text: Exhaust, impressing a new labour mantra, when repeated

indicators.note: to impress is to press in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: eduction is the exhaust of a steam engine

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's slogan repeated until it exhausts everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair's 1996 slogan for New Labour, the UK party, was 'Education, education, education'. Eduction is an old engineering word for exhaust.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair named schooling his three priorities by saying it three times.

clue.text: Nothing disturbs the beauty of some vessels

indicators.note: the letter disturbs the word by breaking into it

parts.note: Venus is the goddess of beauty
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A small thing spoils a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Venous describes veins, the blood vessels returning blood to the heart.

clue.text: Mirror image being shown feels distorted

parts.note: a film being shown is on

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so the word feels is rearranged

explanation.surface: Looking in the mirror, someone feels warped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges the last word into ESELF. 'Mirror image' tempts towards reflection words like 'reversal', but here it simply means the person seen in the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: What a person sees in a mirror is their own self.

clue.text: No, I'm not blue without time off!

indicators.note: off means bad or wrong, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without means losing something, so a letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they are not sad, just without time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' is not a reply but the chemical symbol. 'without' takes T from I'M NOT BLUE, and 'off' rearranges IMNOBLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: No is the chemical symbol of element 102, named after Alfred Nobel.

clue.text: Last to seek dispute, stick up for basic industry

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top
the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or dispute
to gel is to stick together

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for heavy industry after a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole of K, ROW and GEL. 'industry' here means hard work, not manufacturing.
explanation.definitionFit: Legwork is the routine, tiring groundwork, basic hard effort.

clue.text: Winner clutching first of medals, as top

indicators.note: the word clutches the letter inside it

parts.note: an ace is a winning serve in tennis

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A champion grabs a medal and comes out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Acme means the peak or highest point.

clue.text: Seeing scold, Conservative has to rush in to the wardrobe?

parts.note: running into a wardrobe is a way to hide

explanation.surface: Fearing a telling-off, a Tory dives into a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To chide is to rebuke or tell off.

clue.text: Coded message being received in turn, call wheeler outside

parts.note: to cry is to call out

indicators.note: one word goes outside another, holding it

parts.note: a pram, a baby carriage, runs on wheels

indicators.note: in turn means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: got means received

explanation.surface: A message is passed along, each person calling a cyclist outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' makes TOG; 'outside' wraps the baby carriage round it. 'wheeler' is a jokey coinage for anything on wheels, here a pram, not a cyclist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogram is a text written in code or cipher.

clue.text: Us city in which a tramp brought up

indicators.note: in a down light, brought up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: tramp is a slang insult for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: An American town where a vagrant was raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' means US, United States. 'brought up' reverses A and SLUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma, in the United States.

clue.text: Seldom view changes t txt lk ths?

indicators.note: the letters of seldom view change their order

explanation.surface: A rare sight alters a text message shorn of its vowels.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition shows the result: 'to text like this' with every vowel stripped out.
explanation.definitionFit: To disemvowel is to remove the vowels from writing, as done to the clue's last words.

clue.text: Amazing thing that may rise and fall

indicators.note: the word reads the same up or down the grid

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something astonishing goes up and comes down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light the word reads the same going up as going down.
explanation.definitionFit: A wow is a sensational success.

clue.text: Letters at the back of a Russian passport for poet

parts.words: Letters at the back of a Russian
parts.note: many Russian surnames end in -ov, like Ivanov
a passport is a form of ID, identification

explanation.surface: A poet's travel document is from Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman writer of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Smoking habit?

definitions.meaning: a habit is clothing, here a short double-breasted jacket

explanation.definitionFit: Reefer is slang for a joint, and also a close-fitting jacket worn by sailors.

clue.text: Big hitting

definitions.meaning: very large, as in a huge lie

explanation.definitionFit: Whacking means huge in British slang, and also striking something hard.
